note: The compression-spike corpus. The four canonical benchmark applications reuse benchmark/canonical/<App>/payload exactly (benchmark/results/canonical-<App>.json). The seven additional OSS applications are pinned to the artifacts researched on 2026-09-19 (results/oss-apps-research.json holds the full research record). The five IT Tiger applications come from their real release payloads on this machine: the exact staging tree the shipped Inno Setup installer was compiled from where the installer is Inno Setup 7 (innoextract reads Inno Setup up to 6.7 only), or the payload block of the shipped TigerSetup installer where the application already ships with TigerSetup.

apps.name: VSCode
apps.license: Microsoft VS Code licence (proprietary binary; source MIT); payload input only, nothing redistributed

apps.name: GIMP
apps.reason: Not acquired: the only official Windows artifact is gimp-3.2.6-setup.exe (190,358,080 bytes, SHA-256 9337cccb...), an Inno Setup 7.0.0.3 installer. No open unpacker reads Inno Setup 7 (innoextract 1.9 stops at 6.2.2, its master at 6.7.0; 7-Zip has no Inno reader), and the MSIX is a Store-only artifact, so the payload could only be obtained by executing the installer. That is disproportionate for a spike whose corpus already holds a GTK/Python/gettext application of the same shape (Inkscape).

apps.name: WinSCP
apps.note: WinSCP's stable line ships no x64 binary; the portable build is x86. Included as the real release.

apps.name: TigerMarkView

apps.name: TigerWrap
